name: Eliab
overview: Eliab was a male Levite who held the position of second rank gatekeeper, as noted in 1 Chronicles 15:18. His role within the tribe of Levi highlights his service in the religious duties of Israel. There are no additional personal notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Eliab means 'G-d [El] is [my] father,' reflecting a theologically significant Hebrew name. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine relationship.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Eliab as a descendant of Levi, linking him to the priestly tribe responsible for temple service. Beyond this tribal connection, no further family relationships are noted for this individual.
scriptureSignificance: Eliab's significance lies in his role as a Levite gatekeeper, serving in the orderly worship of God. His Levitical lineage and appointed rank illustrate the importance of faithful service in God's house. The meaning of his name underscores a personal acknowledgment of God as Father, fitting for one dedicated to temple duties.
